parsed.summary: `euler_breakdown_R3` states that some smooth, divergence-free initial velocity on ℝ³, all of whose derivatives decay faster than any polynomial, has no global smooth solution of unforced incompressible Euler on [0,∞) with square-integrable velocity and uniformly bounded energy. That is a qualitative global non-existence result, broadly consistent with Theorem 1.1. `exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity` is meant to carry the quantitative content of Theorem 1.1 (compact support, finite lifespan T*, lim sup ‖∇u‖ = ∞, ∫‖curl u‖_∞ = ∞). The most important caveat: that theorem assumes `hbase : (1 : ℕ) = 0`, which is false, so it is vacuously true and certifies nothing.

glossary.note: Junk value 0 at non-differentiable points; it is only used on smooth fields.

glossary.plain: Additionally, for every m and K there is C with |D^m u₀(x)| ≤ C(1+|x|)^{-K}
glossary.note: Weaker than the paper's compact support; it contains C_c^∞.

glossary.plain: (v,p) jointly C^∞ on ℝ³×[0,∞); ∂_t v + (v·∇)v = −∇p and ∇·v = 0 for t ≥ 0; v(·,0) = u₀
glossary.note: The time derivative at t = 0 is one-sided, within [0,∞).

glossary.plain: Global smooth solution with v(t) ∈ L² for each t and sup_t ‖v(t)‖²_{L²} < ∞
L² class of f, or 0 if f ∉ L²
glossary.note: The fallback 0 is only reached where MemLp is not otherwise required.

glossary.plain: On I, v(t) is spatially C^∞, all spatial jets are in L², and t ↦ D^m v(t) is continuous into L² for every m
Euler solution on I in the H^∞ class with strong L² time derivative w; the equation holds at interior times
glossary.standard_concept: H^∞ smooth Euler solution on an interval

glossary.plain: curl v, written with cyclic indices

glossary.note: The paper's blow-up statement concerns ‖∇u‖_∞ alone; including ‖v‖_∞ makes the lim sup = ∞ claim weaker.

lean_claims.plain: There exists u₀ that is smooth, divergence-free and Schwartz-decaying such that no (v,p) is a jointly smooth global solution of unforced Euler on ℝ³×[0,∞) with v(t) ∈ L² for all t and uniformly bounded energy.

Assuming 1 = 0 in ℕ: there exist a compactly supported nonzero datum u₀, a time T* ∈ (0,1], and an H^∞ solution (v,p) on [0,T*) such that (i) closed-interval solutions on [0,T] exist iff T < T*, (ii) the C¹ norm and vorticity integral are finite below T*, (iii) lim sup_{t↑T*} C¹ norm = ∞, (iv) ∫_0^{T*} ‖curl v‖_∞ dt = ∞, and (v) no global finite-energy smooth solution exists. Because the hypothesis is false, the statement is vacuous.

paper_claims.plain: There exists u₀ ∈ C_c,σ^∞(ℝ³) with 0 < T*(u₀) < ∞ whose smooth solution satisfies lim sup_{t↑T*} ‖∇u(t)‖_∞ = ∞ and ∫_0^{T*} ‖curl u(t)‖_∞ dt = ∞.

The content would be roughly equivalent, but the false hypothesis 1 = 0 makes the statement vacuous.
